title: Entities, components and ownership
summary: Build a scene graph and understand how entities, components and groups share transforms and ownership.

blocks.text: What an entity owns

Entity is the base node for geometry, composites, cameras and custom scene nodes. It owns State, transform, paint, material, children and component references. GeometryComponent describes geometry and resources; FragmentComponent describes shading; RendererComponent prepares draw behavior. High-level primitives install compatible components for you.

blocks.text: Read this as an ownership and specialization map: Scene contains entities; each Entity carries a Transform and Paint and can attach components. VectorEntity specializes the base node with vector geometry. Click a named node to open its API reference and inspect its members.
How entity types inherit behavior

Camera, VectorEntity and the other branches below extend Entity. Follow VectorEntity to the geometry types, or select a concrete type to see its ancestors. The arrows describe type inheritance; the parent/child links in your scene describe ownership between instances.
Use the [complete class hierarchy](/class-hierarchy#explorer) to explore engine and library types.
Compare parent axes with world axes
The two parents begin with the same rotation. The cyan dot shifts along its parent’s axis; the amber dot shifts along a world axis. Click a frame to rotate its parent and inspect the difference.
Explore parent and child transforms
Hierarchy and grouping

Use `parent.add(child)` for a spatial hierarchy and `this.add(parent)` for a root. VGroup is a VectorEntity composite. Group is a collection of entities with group animation helpers; it does not extend Entity and is not a scene-graph parent. Static HBox/VBox arrangement positions independent entities without parenting them.
Do not register the same child as both a scene root and a child of another root. Traverse and animate a collection through the ownership model intended for it.
Removal and cleanup

`Scene.remove()` collects descendants, removes matching scene roots, clears scene references and calls `destroy()` on the collected entities. It is a destructive lifecycle operation. `parent.remove(child)` detaches a child without destroying it. `Scene.destroy()` currently shuts down its whole composer, including other scenes hosted by that composer. Follow [lifecycle ownership](/lifecycle-resources) when reusing nodes or composing multiple scenes.

Retained allocator slots, buffers, textures, DOM overlays, update tasks and plugins all have lifetimes. Dispose the object that owns a resource; do not destroy a shared GPU buffer merely because one wrapper stops displaying it.
Visibility, culling and picking

z_index participates in ordering and adds a projected depth bias of z_index × 0.001 in shared vertex helpers. It is not an unlimited painter-order integer: a large bias can move otherwise visible geometry outside the depth clip range. Use small explicit biases when needed and verify the camera/depth configuration.

Rendering visibility, FRUSTUM_CULL, CAST_SHADOW, RECEIVE_SHADOW, RT_ENABLE, layerMask and isPickable serve separate jobs. A visually opaque object is not automatically an interaction target. Rendering state setters typically mark versioned state dirty, while raw typed-array mutation may require explicit refresh or invalidation.

Exact contracts: [Entity](/api-core-entity#entity), [State](/api-core#state), [Component](/api-core#component), [GeometryComponent](/api-components#geometrycomponent), [FragmentComponent](/api-components#fragmentcomponent), [RendererComponent](/api-components#renderercomponent), [Group](/api-core#group), [VGroup](/api-entities-layout#vgroup).
